title: Error Detection
author: Daemen
rules:
Rules:

• Normal sudoku rules apply.

• Hash: Digits in a cage labeled “Hash” cannot repeat. Each Hash cage has an associated Checksum and Parity (see below), and no two Hash cages may have the same Checksum and Parity pair.

• Checksum: The digits in a Hash’s Checksum cage, read left to right, form a two-digit number equal to the sum of the digits in that Hash cage.

• Parity: The digit in a Hash's Parity cage equals the decimal value of the binary number formed by reading the Hash cage’s digits in order (left to right, top to bottom) and replacing each even digit with 0 and each odd digit with 1.

Example:

A Hash cage containing the digits 2, 4, 1, 6, 8 (in that order) sums to 21, so its

Checksum is 2, 1. Its parity string is 00100, which is 4 in decimal, so its Parity digit
is 4. No other Hash cage may have both Checksum 21 and Parity 4.
